Chapter 5: Incentives Shape the World in Unexpected Ways.
Every single day, you’re faced with choices—what you’ll eat, where you’ll work, how you spend your free time.
Most of us like to think we’re making those decisions based on what we really want, or just plain common sense. But, here’s the thing—there’s something working in the background, guiding every move you make. Incentives.
Let me tell you about a group of office workers. Their company decides it’s time to boost productivity, so management rolls out a bonus system. At first, it’s great—people are motivated, everyone’s putting in extra effort, and results climb. But after a while, cracks start to show.
Some employees begin cutting corners, others zero in only on tasks that earn bonuses, and suddenly, teamwork takes a hit. What was meant to encourage better work ends up causing a whole new set of problems.
And this isn’t just an office thing—it happens everywhere.
Picture a city where officials want to reduce traffic accidents. They figure, “Let’s raise the fines for speeding.” Sounds logical, right? Well, drivers just get sneakier. Some come up with clever ways to dodge speed traps, and a few even start bribing officials to avoid tickets. The push to avoid punishment just leads to new ways of breaking the rules.
Even in the world of crime, incentives are at play.
Researchers looking into the lives of sex workers learned that every decision—every risk taken or avoided—comes down to incentives. For many, it’s about money, but just as much about safety and a sense of dignity. When danger goes up and rewards go down, people get creative. They might work together, share tips, or even cooperate with the police to stay safe.
Take the story of one woman who, with options running out, chooses sex work to support her family. She’s careful, picking clients who seem trustworthy and steering clear of risky situations. Over time, she builds a network—people she can count on, ways to stay protected. Her journey shows us that incentives aren’t just about cash. Sometimes, it’s about survival, respect, and hope for something better.
So, what’s the big lesson here?
Incentives are everywhere, quietly shaping the world in ways we rarely notice. When you start to really understand how they work, you can begin to predict what people will do, find smarter solutions, and maybe—even change the world around you.
